result:
I built `note_taker.py` (stdlib only) in the working directory. I tested every subcommand against a temporary notes directory, and they all worked. I didn't test the case where `edit` or `new` opens a real interactive editor. The one earlier hang was my own test, not the script: my shell had `VISUAL` set, which the script uses ahead of `EDITOR`, so it opened an interactive editor. I killed that run and the script worked once I unset `VISUAL`.

**Commands**
- **`new <title> [-t tag]... [-b body] [--no-edit]`** creates a note. The body comes from `--body`, then piped stdin, then `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` (falling back to `vi`). Tags can be repeated or comma-separated.
- **`list` (alias `ls`) `[-t tag]... [-s keyword]`** shows notes newest-first. Several `-t` flags must all match, and tag matching ignores case. `-s` searches title, body and tags, ignoring case.
- **`show <id> [--raw]`** prints a note, or the raw file with `--raw`.
- **`edit <id>`** opens the note in your editor. It refreshes the `updated` timestamp only if you changed something.
- **`delete` (alias `rm`) `<id> [-y]`** asks for confirmation unless you pass `-y`.

**Storage**
- Notes are stored as `~/.note-taker/<slug>.md`, with `title`, `tags`, `created` and `updated` in the frontmatter. Duplicate titles get `-2`, `-3` and so on.
- The `<id>` argument is the filename without `.md`. A unique prefix or substring also works, and an ambiguous one lists the matches.

I added one thing you didn't ask for: setting `NOTE_TAKER_DIR` points the script at a different notes directory, which is how I tested without touching `~/.note-taker/`.

Nothing is committed yet. `note_taker.py` is the only untracked file in the repo.
